unit: Australian federal House of Representatives electoral division, 2025; n expected 150, all divisions not selected by outcome
prior: McGinn & Maruyama (2025), Economic Record 101(334) 275–300, identified causal ballot candidate-count effect in older 2004–2016 settings using redistribution; AEC 2025 participation summary mentions Riverina & Calwell both 13 candidates and informality 11.2% and 10.6%; known prior exposure, NOT NOVEL discovery claim.
R1: Proxy outcome proportion of informal (invalid) ballots among votes cast, not voter intentions or candidate evaluation. Distinguish deliberate blank from accidental errors, no individual effects.
R2: Strong baseline: state and AEC pre-election demographic classification, plus log close-of-rolls enrolment, compare candidate count incremental fit. Do not use 2025 turnout/informal swing as pre-election prediction input.
R3: All 150 divisions fixed before downloading tabular outcomes, but two 13-candidate high-informal examples preexposed via AEC summary. Exploratory independent time-window 2025, NOT temporally blind. No confirmatory p-values.
R4: Remove two pre-exposed divisions, check long-ballot threshold >6 and state/demographic effects; leave-state-out external geographic validation
R5: Only one new independent temporal 2025 AEC dataset; do not repeat D'Hondt or UK650. If source mirror only, no original byte authenticity claim. No new N1 without new mechanism.
I: No individual or party/candidate rating, purely counts of nominations and ballots
A: Does a theoretically relevant ballot-length threshold (>6 nominations, requiring numbering of all candidates) differentiate informal ballot share, and is it robust when excluding pre-exposed 13-candidate outliers?

B.H0: No higher informal with longer ballot
B.Halt: Large association solely two preexposed 13-candidate divisions

C: Compare 7+ vs <=6 groups, predeclared full sample and drop Calwell/Riverina. Use Welch mean comparison, group n, median and within-state stratified mean differences. Do not interpret threshold discontinuity causally: choice of nominations not randomized and legal counting doesn't jump at exactly 6.
F: Polling instructions require numbering every candidate; 7 is descriptive cutoff, not a legal threshold event
G: AEC 2025 informal ballot review 2026 selected high-informality divisions, separate source but selection-biased mechanism evidence
